events.title: The death of Pope St. Nicholas the Great
events.shortBlurb: The last of the three popes surnamed "the Great," who upheld the see of Peter against kings and patriarchs alike, died at Rome…
body: Nicholas I was elected bishop of Rome on 24 April 858, consecrated the same day in St. Peter's in the presence of the Emperor Louis II. Of the whole roll of popes, only three bear in the Annuario the title "the Great" — Leo I, Gregory I, and Nicholas — and he earned it as the most forceful pontiff of the Carolingian age.

He upheld the indissolubility of marriage against Lothair II of Lorraine, who sought to put away his wife Teutberga; he defended the rights of bishops such as Rothad of Soissons against their metropolitans; and he resisted Photius, whose irregular elevation at Constantinople foreshadowed the later schism between East and West. In all these causes he asserted the primacy and the judicial authority of the Roman see over the whole Church.

In Rome he rebuilt and endowed churches and encouraged religious life, keeping himself to a spirit of Christian asceticism. He died on 13 November 867, greatly esteemed by his contemporaries; his cult was reaffirmed by Urban VIII in 1630, and his feast is kept on 13 November.
